value: A NAMESPACE THE ERROR MESSAGE ADVERTISES AND THE RESOLVER REFUSES TRAINS EVERY AUTHOR TO FILE IN THE WRONG PLACE, AND THE MISFILING LOOKS LIKE A HABIT RATHER THAN A DEFECT. `entity_key_namespaces` has listed `tool:` and `workflow:` as live record-subject namespaces since run 35, and the unknown-entity refusal names them -- but `_reference_resolvable` handled only `function:` and `tu:` plus keys ALREADY PRESENT in the entity table, and entity rows are auto-created from record anchors. So the first record to write `subject: tool:probe` was refused as an unknown entity, and every author fell back to `project:gdl`. 130 accepted records now sit there, tool-behaviour laws among them, where `gdlmem tool <name>` could not see them: `tool probe` returned 11 tool_catalog entries and ZERO laws, while 6 laws about probe.py's own behaviour sat under THREE different foreign subjects (tu:game/game/combat, tu:game/sys/memcard, project:gdl). This is the THIRD recurrence of the same item in the tool queue. THE FIX IS TO GIVE THE NAMESPACE A VOCABULARY, not to document it harder: tool_catalog already holds a row keyed `tool:<slug>` for every tools/gdl source plus every reviewed tool record, so resolving `tool:` against that table makes the advertised namespace true. GENERAL FORM: an advertised affordance with no implementation behind it is worse than an absent one, because the workaround it forces becomes the corpus's convention and then reads as the authors' preference. When a queue item recurs a third time, check whether the thing being asked for EXISTS at all before asking why nobody uses it. COROLLARY, measured while building the bridge back to the misfiled records: bridging on `asserted_by` pulled 33 laws about combat.c and gauntworld into `tool probe`, because asserted_by names the tool that MEASURED a law, not the law's subject. Provenance is not aboutness.
